text:
hana: Hey team — day 1 and I'm running into a wall. asdf plugin-add python and node both fail with "SSL: certificate verify failed" when on the office VPN. Also VS Code terminal doesn't pick up my `~/.local.env` exports. Any quick steps? :wave:

leo: Welcome Hana! Most likely corporate TLS interception + env propagation across GUI apps. Quick plan: 1) add corp root CA to system trust store, 2) run a local auth proxy if PAC/NTLM is used, 3) ensure envs are exported in files GUI shells source (zprofile/.profile).

mai: For the CA on mac: put the `corp.crt` in Downloads then `sudo security add-trusted-cert -d -r trustRoot -k /Library/Keychains/System.keychain ~/Downloads/corp.crt`. Restart apps. On Linux add it to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and run `sudo update-ca-certificates`.

hana: we use an auto PAC file for proxy rules and AD credentials. How do you handle NTLM auth?

leo: cntlm is our go-to. Install via Homebrew (`brew install cntlm`) or apt, configure `/usr/local/etc/cntlm.conf` with your domain and hashed password, run `brew services start cntlm`, then `export HTTP_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:3128` and `HTTPS_PROXY` too. For WSL/Docker you might need to expose the Windows-side proxy IP.

mai: Important: set both uppercase and lowercase env vars: `export HTTP_PROXY=...` and `export http_proxy=...` because different tools respect different names. Put those exports in `~/.zprofile` so GUI apps started via Finder/Spotlight inherit them after a logout/login, or launch VS Code from a terminal with `code .` to inherit live envs.

hana: my `~/.local.env` has secrets (NPM_TOKEN) and is already gitignored. Why doesn't VS Code see it?

leo: VS Code's integrated terminal will only see what's in the environment of the VS Code process. If you launch VS Code from the Dock it won't read your shell rc. Options: 1) launch from terminal `code .`, 2) move proxy/token exports to `~/.zprofile` or `/etc/launchd.conf` (mac) via a launch agent, or 3) use VS Code Remote > Container feature and mount secrets into the container. We recommend direnv + `~/.local.env` and the direnv VS Code extension — then VS Code respects direnv if extension is enabled.

mai: also ensure `eval "$(asdf init -)"` is early in your `~/.zshrc`/`~/.bash_profile` so shims are in PATH. If `which node` points to `/usr/bin/node` or a brew path, run `brew unlink node` then open a fresh shell. `asdf reshim` can help too after installs.

hana: encountering gpg errors when installing node via asdf: "Can't check signature: No public key". Any tips?

leo: Run the importer script the node plugin provides: `~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring` (may require `gpg` to be installed: `brew install gnupg`). If curl can't fetch the key due to proxy, fix CA/proxy first.

infra-bot: Heads up: onboarding KB updated with "proxy + asdf" steps and a sample `~/.local.env` template: https://internal.redwood/docs/onboarding/proxy-asdf-template :page_with_curl:

hana: great. One last thing: are there recommended defaults for dotfiles so new hires don't accidentally leak tokens? I have a dotfiles fork and want to push my personalizations.

mai: We keep secrets out of repo with a `.secrets.example` template and require a local `~/.local.env` that's in `.gitignore`. The dotfiles repo has a pre-commit hook to block accidentally adding env files. Add a README snippet that shows how to get tokens with 1Password CLI (example: `eval $(op signin) && op item get "redwood/dev-tokens" --fields token > ~/.local.env`) so it's reproducible for others.

leo: Also add a small `CONTRIBUTING.md` note telling contributors how to handle local secrets and to never paste token values in PR descriptions or public issues. We rotate any leaked tokens immediately but it's good to avoid risk.

hana: Thanks all — I'll add the CA, run cntlm, put env exports in zprofile, and try launching VS Code from terminal. Will ping if anything else blocks. :pray:
